title: Lucena: building the bridge

D0.outcome: Explains the Lucena idea: rook and pawn on the seventh with the king in front, won by building a bridge that shelters the king from checks.

D1.outcome: Plays the bridge technique from the standard position and names each step.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled rook endings, recognises winning Lucena-type positions and the ones that are not (the king not cut off), and says which side is to move.

D3.outcome: Plays out against the tablebase-backed opponent with a move budget, and knows when the cut-off by a single file is too narrow.

misconceptions: Any rook ending with a pawn on the seventh wins.
sources: sources/sheets/nimzowitsch_my-system.md §4 idea 23 (shelter and bridge-building; matches the standard technique, to check)
docs/curriculum-map-v1.1.md §4 (a Lucena-type position verified a win)
conditions: The attacker's king stands in front of the pawn on the queening side, the enemy king is cut off, and the rook builds a bridge on a line that shelters the king from checks.
Provisional cut-off criterion from a book ending: the enemy king is cut off by two files and the pawn reaches the fourth rank before the defender's rook can start checking; unverified, flagged CHECK.
condition_sources: Nimz #23 (b); a Lucena-type position verified a win, MAP11 §4
contrasts: The defender's rook is behind with the move.
The enemy king is not cut off, so the same pieces draw.
